verdict.justification: A is the more implementation-ready package, retaining the reference’s triggers, RACI, required form fields, approval sequence, and audit requirements while providing clearer operational controls. Its separate Fast-Track and Full Review approval tables avoid B’s form-level contradiction: B says “Fast-Track: PM and QA only” but labels PM Lead signoff “Always, after all required approvals.” B also instructs “If no trigger applies, no CR is needed,” which conflicts with its own requirement to document and log Fast-Track changes. A handles decision tracking substantially better, explicitly stating “Escalated is not a closing status” and distinguishing approval from implementation completion and closure. Its form and tracker also capture attachment versions, archive references, resubmission history, and escalation resolution more thoroughly than B’s simpler templates. A does introduce proposed policies beyond the source, including treatment of sub-threshold budget overages and two-day adjustments, but identifies these as assumptions requiring confirmation; overall, it would require less substantive rework before routing.
